neighbours.label: a conjunction ('For', 'And', 'Yet', ', for') opening a line or clause of verse
fire:
The candle gutters in the cold,
For all the oil is spent and old.

I wandered long beside the shore,
And heard the grey waves sigh once more.
My heart is heavy, friend, for I must leave thee now.

The winter took the garden bare,
Yet still a rose was blooming there.

Speak softly, love, for night has ears,
And every star records our tears.

The road is long and I am weak,
For I have walked a year this week.
She gave her hand, and therefore I am bound.

The bells of evening toll and fade,
Yet in my dreams their music played.
quiet:
The candle gutters in the cold,
Its little flame is thin and old.

I wandered long beside the shore,
The grey waves sighing evermore.
My heart is heavy, friend; I leave thee now.

The winter took the garden bare,
One rose was blooming even there.

Speak softly, love, the night has ears,
The stars record our many tears.

The road is long and I am weak,
I walked a year, it seems, this week.
She gave her hand; I am bound to her.

The bells of evening toll and fade,
In dreams I hear the song they played.

notes: Card: line-initial 'For'/'And'/'Yet' in Shakespeare and Dickinson, plus ', for I must'. Near misses are the same verse lines without the opening conjunction.
